patterns.comment: A character name is either a bare identifier, or a double/single-quoted string - the quoted form lets a name contain spaces or symbols that wouldn't otherwise be valid (e.g. join "John Smith" left).
patterns.name: entity.name.character.dtl

patterns.comment: Optional mood/emotion tag right after the character name, e.g. 'join John (default) left'. Reuses the same variable.other.emotion.dtl scope as extra_data="set ..." below and the dialogue-speaker mood tag in #dialogue, so all three read as one consistent concept in the theme. The lookbehind's character-name alternation mirrors entity.name.character.dtl above so a quoted name is recognized here too.

patterns.name: variable.language.all.dtl
patterns.comment: Was previously '^\s*leave\s+(--All--)', which required the match to start at the very beginning of the line - but keyword.control.command.dtl (listed above) always wins that tie and consumes just 'leave', so the '^' anchor could never fire again afterward and --All-- silently lost its color. A lookbehind sidesteps the anchor entirely.

flow.comment: if / else / elif / set / label / jump / not / and / or / in all share keyword.control.flow.dtl so a theme colors them identically. label/jump additionally tag their target name with entity.name.label.dtl, mirroring how #commands tags character names after join/update/leave.

patterns.comment: label Name (Display Name) - like Dialogic, the name is everything up to an optional (Display Name), so it can contain spaces. Stops before a trailing #id: translation id, which #translationid colors.

jump label, jump Timeline/label or jump Timeline/ - the timeline part is everything up to the last '/', like Dialogic. A {variable} target is left to #variables, and a (wrong) trailing #id: to #translationid.

variables.comment: {path.to.value} — braces and dot-separated segments get their own scopes so a theme can shade the path differently from plain text.

global_references.comment: A bare identifier immediately followed by '.' and another identifier - the shape of a global reference, e.g. 'Global.apply_tint()' inside do/if/elif/while (Global can be an autoload singleton or a class_name-declared script; DTL/Dialogic doesn't distinguish syntactically, so neither does this). Purely structural, matching regardless of whether the name is a real declared global - the same spirit as support.function.dtl below already coloring ANY identifier-before-'(' the same way. Placed after #dialogue/#narration in the top-level patterns list so ordinary prose containing a stray 'word.word' (e.g. 'Mr.Smith') is still claimed by them first - narration's begin pattern matches at column 0 for any qualifying line, which always wins over a match starting later, and ties are broken by list order in narration's favor.

patterns.comment: A member followed by '(' is a function call: Global.apply_tint()
patterns.name: support.function.dtl

patterns.comment: A member itself followed by '.member' is a nested type - in practice a named enum: Global.TimeId.CHAP2_R1
patterns.name: entity.name.type.enum.dtl

patterns.comment: An ALL_CAPS member is a constant or an enum value, following GDScript's naming convention: Global.MAX_HEARTS, Global.TimeId.CHAP2_R1
patterns.name: constant.other.enum-member.dtl

patterns.comment: Anything else after the '.' is a property: Global.hearts
patterns.name: variable.other.member.dtl

balises.comment: BBCode-style rich text tags used inside player-facing text: [b]bold[/b], [i]italic[/i], [u]underline[/u], [s]strikethrough[/s], and any other custom effect tag like [MyEffect]text[/MyEffect]. Each opening tag only matches if a lookahead confirms its matching closer exists later on the SAME line - if no closer is found, nothing highlights here at all (the brackets stay plain text), so the tag's highlighting is always strictly the region between the two tags and never spills onto the rest of the line. An unclosed tag is instead caught by the whole-line diagnostic in extension.js. Each rule includes #balises itself so tags can nest/combine, e.g. [b][i]bold italic[/i][/b] - the theme has matching combined-scope rules for every 2-tag pairing so both effects actually render together; 3+ levels of nesting will fall back to showing just the innermost tag's style.

patterns.name: markup.custom-balise.dtl
patterns.comment: Any other BBCode tag or personalized balise, e.g. [Shake]text[/Shake], with optional parameters after the name - [color=red], [shake level=5], [wave amp=50 freq=5] - colored like attributes inside the tag. Reserved bracket commands (wait, audio, signal...) are excluded via the lookahead so they keep using #options as before, and like the other rules it only matches when the closer exists on the same line, so Dialogic's own closer-less text effects ([pause=1.5], [speed=2]...) are left alone.

dialogue.comment: Speaker line 'Name: text [inline=options] #id:xyz'. The spoken text is a begin/end region so inline markup like [pause=1.5], [b]bold[\b], and {variable} references still highlight.

patterns.comment: Speaker name is a bare identifier, or a double/single-quoted string so it can contain spaces/symbols (e.g. "John Smith": ...). The reserved-keyword exclusion only needs to guard the bare form - a quoted string can never collide with a flow keyword.
patterns.name: entity.name.character.dtl

patterns.comment: Optional mood/emotion tag between the speaker name and the colon, e.g. 'John (angry): blabla'. Same variable.other.emotion.dtl scope as join/update's mood tag and extra_data="set ...". Lookbehind mirrors the speaker-name alternation above so a quoted speaker's mood tag is recognized too.

narration.comment: A line with no 'Character:' prefix is still spoken/narrated text in Dialogic - a nameless speaker gets the same treatment as a named one. Reuses #dialogue's text scope and nested patterns. The negative lookaheads exclude anything that is actually a comment, choice, bracket command, or flow/command keyword line, so those keep their own dedicated highlighting instead of being swallowed as narration.

choices.comment: '- choice text | [if ...] [else=...] #id:xyz'. The leading dash is punctuation. Only the choice wording gets the choice color and stops before |, #, or the end of the line.

signals.comment: [signal arg_type="dict" arg="{...}"] - kept as its own repository (rather than folded into #options) so it can be themed as a distinct 'event' scope.

signal_dictionary.comment: A dictionary signal argument, arg="{"Effect":"Rain","Amount":100}" - colored like JSON (keys, string/number/boolean values, punctuation) instead of one long string. Works whether the inner quotes are escaped (\") or not (Dialogic's editor writes them unescaped). Only a value starting with '{' gets this treatment; any other arg stays a plain #strings string.

text_effects.comment: Dialogic's own text effects inside text (not Godot BBCode): [pause=0.5], [speed=2], [lspeed=0.05], [signal=arg], [portrait=happy], [mood=angry], [extra_data=set Head/Happy], [aa], [ns], [nrs], [input], [n], [n+]. They have no closer. Conditional text [if {x} a/b] is left to #options, which already colors its 'if'.

random_selection.comment: Dialogic's random selection text modifier: <Hey!/Hello!/Hi!> shows one of the options at random. Only matches when there's at least one '/' between the angle brackets.

options.comment: Generic '[key=value key2="value2"]' bracket block used by commands, choices and inline dialogue markup (extra_data, animation, pause, if/else, alt_text...).

patterns.comment: extra_data="set Emotion/Happy" - only the 'set ...' shape gets the emotion scope on its payload, so a theme can make Emotion/Happy read the same way as a mood tag like 'John (happy):'. Anything not starting with 'set ' stays a plain string.
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.dtl
